status.en: 202 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 202 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to target civilians and security forces in Plateau, killing a soldier and stealing weapons at checkpoints and abducting students and worshippers, while ISWAP leaders and a shura council member were killed by troops in Borno. The attacks on worshippers in Kaduna resulted in seventeen deaths in captivity and four remain held. A drone strike by ISWAP in Borno killed two soldiers and injured thirteen. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å angripe sivile og sikkerhetsstyrker i Plateau, dreper en soldat og stjeler våpen ved sjekkpunkter og bortfører studenter og tilbedere, mens ISWAP-ledere og et medlem av shura-rådet ble drept av tropper i Borno. Angrepene på tilbedere i Kaduna resulterte i sytten døde i fangenskap og fire er fortsatt holdt. Et droneangrep fra ISWAP i Borno drepte to soldater og såret tretten. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
